newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rate woes seen keeping German share trade uneven.
newsitem.headline: Rate woes seen keeping German share trade uneven.

text.p: German shares were trading slightly lower early on Wednesday, as worries about a possible interest rate rise weighed on market activity.
"People have become quite unsettled," said a Frankfurt trader. "With the dollar trading at these levels, it seems perfectly probable the Bundesbank will act."
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was down 7.60 points at 4,318.36 points at 0811 GMT, while September DTB DAX futures were down 23.5 at 4,329.5.
The main events of the morning, the release of jobless data and the Bundesbank's weekly repo tender, had little impact.
Germany's seasonally adjusted jobless total rose by 17,000 in July, against average forecasts for a rise of 4,000.

Meanwhile the Bundesbank injected a higher-than-expected volume of funds into the market -- adding a net 2.6 billion marks -- at its weekly tender, a move which dealers said argued against a rate hike in the near future.
But dealers also said the dollar's continued ascent against the mark was a strong influence in favour of an imminent rate hike.
"This is a risky time. It is not a time to commit yourself to this market," a dealer said.

The few clear advancers of the day included sportswear manufacturer Adidas AG, which reported early on Wednesday that its first-half profit jumped to 238 million marks from 184 million marks -- at the top end of forecasts.
The shares hit a high of 223 marks before settling back to 218 marks, still up 0.6 percent.
